planning.title: Before the first brick.
planning.intro: Nexus Terminal — a multi-level metro station study on Avenida da Boavista, Porto, Portugal.
sections: The problem
The feasibility study examines gaps in public transport, reliance on private vehicles, transfer congestion, and pedestrian access along the Boavista corridor.
My contribution

Six months of pre-construction work covered architectural, structural, and MEP coordination using BIM and Navisworks; Primavera P6 schedules supported 4D sequencing. Model-based takeoffs and Bluebeam validation informed cost planning.
Estimation

The documented workflow moves from a conceptual estimate using gross area and RSMeans to drawing-based quantities, a design-development baseline, and a CSI MasterFormat breakdown. The portfolio lists a total estimated project cost of $60,082,987; this is a study estimate, not a delivered contract value.
Scheduling & risk

The source programme contains approximately 300 activities, about 100 identified as critical, and a 530-day duration. Its risk discussion covers imported curtain-wall procurement and weather-sensitive excavation. The summary and schedule show different finish dates, so no single completion date is asserted here.
Design & environmental response

The proposal connects a high-capacity transit hub with its urban context. The feasibility study identifies walkability, cycling, public transport access, and green corridors as intended benefits; these are design intentions rather than measured outcomes.
Deliverables & outcome

A feasibility study, coordinated model views, plans and sections, a detailed estimate, a Primavera P6 programme, and critical-path documentation make the relationship between scope, cost, and time reviewable. The portfolio records a 260,000 sq. ft. gross built-up area and design-build delivery strategy.

architecture.title: Clinical clarity. Human warmth.
architecture.intro: A 4,000 sq. ft. eye and dental healthcare center balancing clinical function, retail, and patient comfort.
sections: The problem
Bring clinical services, an eyewear retail zone, circulation, and a children's play area into one coherent healthcare environment.
The design response
Clear zoning and circulation organize the patient journey. A restrained, warm material palette supports an approachable setting while maintaining the clarity required by clinical spaces.
My role

Led design development from concept through pre-construction coordination, working with the principal architect, clients, and consultants. Developed presentation sets and coordinated design iterations and permit support.
Technical & project controls

Coordinated medical-equipment zoning with architectural, MEP, and HVAC requirements. Prepared BOQs, bid packages, and cost analyses; managed 15+ vendors and suppliers and tracked RFIs, submittals, and QA/QC documentation.
Delivery & outcome

The portfolio describes design-bid-build delivery and a functional, patient-focused environment. The source drawings and images show the relationship between clinical areas, reception, retail displays, and material choices.
Context
Professional healthcare and commercial-interior work in Yelahanka, Bangalore. A project-specific completion date and software list are not given in the project pages.

resilience.title: A dialogue with the valley.
resilience.intro: A boutique hospitality resort on approximately two acres in the hill station of Yercaud, Tamil Nadu.
sections: The context
The portfolio places the site along an elevated cliff edge, with panoramic valley views and sunset-facing orientations.
The architectural response

Guest spaces and hospitality interiors establish a visual relationship with the surrounding landscape. The presented views emphasize timber, woven textures, planting, and open connections to the valley.
Process & documentation

The portfolio includes architectural plans and a sequence of guest-room, restaurant, and public-space views. The resume describes assisting a principal architect on a two-acre boutique resort, including drawings, FF&E layouts, and interior elevations.
Delivery & evidence

The project sheet lists design-bid-build as the delivery method. A completion date, measured environmental performance, and a project-specific software list are not stated; the images document the design presentation.
resilience.source: Source: portfolio pages 31–33 and related hospitality experience on page 4. The source heading spells the location ‘Yercud’; body text identifies Yercaud.

miami.title: Plan the complexity.
miami.intro: Bank and Office Tower, Miami, Florida — site logistics, quantity takeoff, cost estimation, and scheduling for a proposed development.
sections: My contribution
The stated role covers site logistics coordination, quantity takeoffs, cost estimation, and construction scheduling across the pre-construction and planning phases.
Site strategy
The logistics plan places a luffing-jib tower crane, two material-storage zones, temporary worker facilities, and clearly identified entry and exit points within a constrained development site.
Cost & time
The source summary lists a $147,387,115 project estimate, 714-day programme, and design-bid-build strategy. These are proposed study parameters, not the value or duration of a completed commission.
The deliverables

Architectural plans, site logistics, staffing and cost sheets, and schedule extracts connect the tower proposal to a delivery strategy. The source estimate contains illustrative personnel names, so it is treated as a planning exercise rather than an actual staffing record.
gallery: Site logistics and illustrative estimating sheet
miami.source: Source: portfolio pages 11–15. No completed-project or independent LEED-certification claim is made.

controls.title: Make performance legible.
controls.intro: A reporting archive that links the baseline programme to resources, expenditure, risk, and earned value.
sections: The baseline

The report presents a 224-day construction plan with preparation, construction blocks A–C, and final phases. Its stated budget is approximately $1.21 million; these figures describe the source analysis, not a newly verified live project.
The process
WBS structuring, activity sequencing, resource and cost loading, and baseline comparisons connect the Gantt programme to time-phased labor, materials, and equipment.
Reporting
The archive includes workload analysis, resource assignments, monthly cost reports, cumulative labor curves, a risk register, earned-value dashboards, and schedule-check outputs.
What the analysis surfaces

The source discusses resource over-allocation, early cost overruns, and performance deviations in its examples. These provide a basis for identifying where planning and corrective action are needed; no unsupported savings or delivery improvement is claimed.

sports.title: A spine for collective activity.
sports.intro: Multipurpose Sports Complex — an architectural thesis connecting sports, training, recreation, and public space.
sections: The problem
The thesis addresses a need for sporting infrastructure and public access to facilities in Bangalore, with indoor sports, an aquatic complex, training, and supporting uses.
The concept

The human spine becomes a planning analogy: a connecting circulation system links distinct facilities into one composition. Public and service areas sit closer to access roads; curved pathways and organic massing respond to the landscape.
Technical development

The portfolio documents a 28-acre site, an indoor stadium and training center, a swimming complex, and an administration block. Plans, column layouts, sections, and an exploded structural diagram explain the spatial and structural organization.
The outcome

A thesis proposal developed through site analysis, concept sketches, massing studies, plans, sections, and visualizations. Environmental thinking is expressed through landscape integration and orientation; measured performance and built completion are not claimed.

motorcycle.title: From shell to working system.
motorcycle.intro: A 24,300 sq. ft. commercial service facility integrating a workshop, retail and café areas, and offices.
sections: The challenge
Transform a bare shell into a coordinated service environment, balancing workshop operations, customer circulation, equipment requirements, and public-facing spaces.
My role

Led pre-construction, coordination, procurement, and execution across design-build delivery. Collaborated with architectural, structural, and MEP teams and managed contractors, vendors, and suppliers.
Technical response
Integrated OEM equipment with building services and layout constraints, developed shop drawings and technical layouts, and resolved site coordination issues through stakeholder alignment.
Delivery & outcome

The source records a $2.6 million budget and delivery within budget and ahead of schedule. Its resume and case study give different day counts, so the website intentionally omits a numerical early-completion claim.
